object_description: five-building campus ensemble around a central square
design_condition: Five buildings occupy the planning perimeter to complete the city block, respond to neighboring building heights, and form a central campus square connected by internal alleys and a boulevard.

positive.statement: The clear and comprehensible setting of the five buildings is based on a sensitive analysis of the prevailing context.

position.rationale: Perimeter buildings and varied heights are visible around the central square in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The passage and central internal square support the campus idea and create high-quality additional open space.

position.rationale: The open central court is clearly legible between the surrounding building masses in the top view.

positive.statement: The individual buildings and their assigned uses are organized and structured in a comprehensible manner.

position.rationale: Distinct building blocks are identifiable, while internal use assignments are not visible.

positive.statement: The supporting structure has a very high proportion of wood and is carefully processed.

position.rationale: The structural system is not distinguishable, so the marker uses an upper perimeter building surface.

positive.statement: The facade is carefully and precisely crafted.

position.rationale: A visible outer facade edge is selected on the east side of the perimeter ensemble.

negative.statement: The flexibility of the floors is not optimal and is relatively limited, particularly because of the deep floor plans and wide supports.

position.target: deep floor plans and wide supports
position.rationale: Deep interior planning and supports are not directly visible; the marker references a broad perimeter floor region.

negative.statement: The assignment of faculties to individual buildings is not completely convincing operationally and does not promote cross-disciplinary work.

position.target: assignment of faculties to individual buildings
position.rationale: Separate building volumes are visible, but faculty allocation and operational relationships are internal.

negative.statement: It is very doubtful whether the underground transport network works geometrically and it will likely require more space.

position.rationale: The underground network is absent from the sample; the marker follows the front access edge.

negative.statement: The facade appears more like an office or administrative building than a technical university.

position.rationale: The criticism concerns external identity, anchored to a clearly visible outer facade.

negative.statement: After the second stage, the open space loses some of its generosity and power.

position.target: open space after the second stage
position.rationale: The later-stage open-space condition is anchored to the visible court and adjoining internal alleys.
